newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-BAILEY, JOHNSON SPAR OVER WHO'S THE BEST.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BAILEY, JOHNSON SPAR OVER WHO'S THE BEST.

text.p: Canadian 100 meters world record holder Donovan Bailey on Tuesday declared himself the fastest man in history and branded "a joke" his June showdown with American superstar Michael Johnson to decide who is faster.

"I've become the fastest human that ever walked the planet," Bailey, the Olympic 100 meters gold medalist, told Atlanta Games 200- and 400 meters champion Johnson during a teleconference as they hyped their $1 million 150 meter match race in Toronto's SkyDome on June 1.

"If there was going to be a fastest man in the world title....you would not be part of this race," taunted Bailey, who set the 100-meter world record of 9.84 seconds in Atlanta while reaching a top speed of 27.1 miles per hour (43.6 kph).
"You are not even top-10 ranked in the U.S. in the 100 meters, therefore at 23 miles per hour, you might get out of the quarter-finals of the Olympics in the 100," Bailey told Johnson.
"So now in the Olympic Games, gold medals, silver medals and bronze medals are being given out based on how many miles per hour you run?" Johnson injected.
"No, that's what your speed is about, FASTEST," Bailey replied.
"You're talking to a guy who has been in the sport for two years. You're starting to see the immaturity," Johnson said of Bailey.
"No," responded the Canadian, "it's called what I have done. You, or nobody else in the sport, has never done what I have done in their first three years on the international circuit."
"There's always a world record holder, there's always a gold medalist," retorted Johnson.
But Bailey, who has restored Canadian pride in the sport, said: "There is absolutely no discussion who the fastest man in the world is.
"This is actually a joke as the fastest man in the world contest," he said of the made-for-television event.
"If I was going to do that, I would be running against Frankie Fredericks, who was second in the 100 metres (at Atlanta) or Ato Boldon."
Johnson said that he didn't think he had to prove to anyone "that I am the fastest man in the world or any of those things."

Nonetheless, Johnson, who some thought earned the world's fastest man title with his astounding 200-meter world record of 19.32 seconds at Atlanta Games, guaranteed that he would beat Bailey in the internationally televised event that also will likely include head-to-head competition between Olympic stars in the pole vault, high jump, high hurdles and women's sprints.
Johnson said he originally wanted to include Fredericks, Boldon, Briton Linford Christie and Carl Lewis in the 150-meter race.
"I thought that was a great concept," Johnson said. "But by no means do I mind a head-to-head race. I think it's a great idea."
